version.changelog: Soften SKILL.md wording to reduce false-positive prompt-injection warnings while keeping the workflow intact.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: ui-craft-pro
Version: 0.1.4

The ui-craft-pro skill bundle is a comprehensive UI/UX design assistant designed to help AI agents generate design systems and implementation patterns. The core logic in scripts/core.py and scripts/design_system.py implements a local BM25 search engine over a large set of UI/UX datasets (CSVs) and provides structured design recommendations. While the skill has the capability to write documentation files to the local 'design-system/' directory, this behavior is entirely consistent with its stated purpose of generating project-specific design systems. No evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or prompt injection was found; the code is well-structured and the data contains legitimate design guidelines and code snippets.

llm.summary: The skill’s files and CLI instructions match its UI-design purpose, but a prompt-injection detection in SKILL.md and truncated content create ambiguity — inspect the full SKILL.md and scripts before trusting autonomous use.

dimensions.detail: Name, description, CSV data, and Python scripts (search.py, core.py, design_system.py) all align with a local design-reference + design-system-generation tool for UI work. No unrelated credentials, binaries, or install steps are requested, which is proportionate to the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to run included Python scripts and to use the local data/ references — that is within scope. However the static pre-scan flagged a 'system-prompt-override' pattern in the SKILL.md and some SKILL.md content is truncated in the package listing; this could indicate prompt-manipulation instructions embedded in the runtime instructions. You should review the full SKILL.md for any lines that attempt to override system prompts, inject new system-level instructions, or ask the agent to ignore platform rules.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec or external download — all code and data are bundled locally in the skill. That lowers install-time risk because nothing is fetched from arbitrary URLs. The presence of Python scripts means runtime execution will occur, but no installer or remote code fetch is requested.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, no credentials, and no config-path access. The bundled data files and scripts explain the functionality; there are no obvious requests for unrelated secrets or cloud credentials.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Flags show always:false and default autonomous invocation allowed. The skill does not request elevated persistence or modifications to other skills. This is typical for a user-invocable utility and does not by itself increase concern.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to be a coherent, local UI design helper (search + design-system generation + guidance). However: 1) Open and read the complete SKILL.md file — look for any instructions that tell the agent to change its system prompt, ignore safety rules, or send data elsewhere. 2) Inspect the included Python scripts (search.py, core.py, design_system.py, _sync_all.py) for network calls (requests, urllib, socket, subprocess calling curl), filesystem access beyond the skill folder, or code that transmits data. 3) If you plan to allow autonomous invocation, consider testing the skill in a sandboxed agent first (no network, limited filesystem access). 4) If you’re not comfortable reviewing the code yourself, ask the publisher for a short security statement or refuse installation. The single scanner finding is concerning but not decisive — manual review of the truncated SKILL.md and scripts will resolve the ambiguity.
llm.findings: [system-prompt-override] unexpected: A pre-scan detected a prompt-injection pattern in SKILL.md content. Overriding system prompts or instructing the agent to ignore platform rules is unrelated to a UI design tool and should be treated as suspicious until you inspect the full SKILL.md. The excerpt shown does not obviously contain an override, so this may be a false positive — but the truncated content must be reviewed.
